assumptions: Assumes the system does not clearly inform the child about parental access rights, events, or policy conditions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact unawareness subtree may differ.

title: Non-compliance with consent, custody, or educational privacy obligations
description: Processing the parent's request for the child's grades may violate applicable privacy rules if the portal lacks a valid legal basis, does not honor age-related rights, fails to reflect custody restrictions, or retains/accesses data beyond permitted purposes.
assumptions: Assumes jurisdiction-specific educational/privacy obligations apply and may require dynamic authorization based on parental rights and child age/status.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate from memory because non-compliance trees vary by catalog version.

title: Repudiation of grade-access requests or disclosures
description: If the portal does not maintain adequate evidence of who requested the grades, which child record was accessed, and what was disclosed, the parent or the portal may later deny having made or served the request. This impairs accountability for privacy-relevant access.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient audit logging, weak session binding, or inadequate integrity protection for access records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact non-repudiation subtree may differ.

title: Excessive disclosure of student educational records to the parent
description: The portal may display more of the child's educational record than is necessary for the parent's purpose, such as detailed feedback, full submission history, or grades beyond the relevant period, causing unnecessary disclosure of the student's personal data.
assumptions: Assumes the parent does not always need the full breadth or granularity of grades, feedback, and submission history presented by the portal.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on over-disclosure/minimisation concerns; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: Portal shares student data with a parent without valid authorization or expectation alignment
description: If the portal sends the child's grades, feedback, and submission history to a person recorded as a parent without verifying legal authority, custody status, or the student's reasonable expectations, the disclosure may be unexpected or unlawful from the student's perspective.
assumptions: Assumes parental access rights can vary by age of student, custody arrangements, school policy, or jurisdiction.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for unawareness/expectation mismatch around secondary disclosure to parents.

title: Interception of grades and feedback in transit identifies the child
description: If the data flow is insufficiently protected in transit, an eavesdropper could observe grades, teacher feedback, or submission history and directly identify the child and their educational performance.
assumptions: Assumes transport protection could be absent, downgraded, or bypassed in some contexts.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from content observed on the flow.

title: Flow metadata can link parent and child relationship
description: Even if content is protected, metadata about the portal session or response pattern may reveal that a specific parent is accessing a specific child's school record, linking the identities and relationship of parent and student.
assumptions: Assumes observable metadata such as account identifiers, URLs, timing, or network endpoints can be correlated.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via communication metadata.

title: Parent may further disclose or expose the child's school information after receipt
description: Once received, the parent may store, forward, screenshot, print, or verbally share the child's grades, feedback, and submission history with others, causing onward disclosure beyond the original context.
assumptions: Assumes the destination is outside the school's direct technical control and may use unmanaged devices or channels.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure caused by recipient-side handling; exact subtree may differ.

title: Parent cannot be held accountable for misuse or onward sharing
description: If the system does not provide adequate logging, notice, or binding of access to the specific parent account, the parent may later deny having accessed or shared the child's educational data, reducing accountability for privacy-relevant actions.
assumptions: Assumes limited auditability or weak attribution of portal access at the recipient side.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance/non-accountability style concern; exact mapping may vary.

title: Identification of administrator or affected users via account-management data in transit
description: Names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationship updates sent on this flow can directly identify the administrator performing the action and the students/parents whose accounts or links are being created, modified, or disabled if the transmission is observed or insufficiently protected.
assumptions: Assumes the flow may be observable by intermediaries or logged at network boundaries with payload visibility.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for direct identification from data content; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Linkability of family relationships and administrative actions from transmitted relationship data
description: Parent-child links, combined with names, emails, and roles, allow observers of the flow to correlate multiple records and infer which individuals belong to the same family, as well as connect repeated administrative actions to the same households or accounts.
assumptions: Assumes repeated transmissions or access to multiple messages/metadata over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability through shared identifiers and relationship attributes; exact node id may differ.

title: Disclosure of sensitive account and relationship data in transit
description: The flow contains personal data and relationship information. If intercepted, exposed through weak transport protection, or captured in intermediary logs, unauthorized parties could learn names, emails, roles, account status changes, and parent-child relationships.
assumptions: Assumes transport or intermediary protections may be insufficient, or debugging/proxy infrastructure may capture content.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for disclosure of data in transit.

title: Linkability of users and households within the portal
description: On receipt, the portal can store and correlate names, emails, roles, account lifecycle events, and parent-child links, enabling linkage of student, parent, and administrator records across transactions and over time beyond what is necessary for the immediate account-management task.
assumptions: Assumes the portal retains historical events or combines these records with other portal datasets.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for recipient-side correlation/linkage; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may vary.

title: Identification of individuals through stored account and relationship records
description: The portal receives directly identifying attributes and relationship mappings that can identify administrators, parents, and students, especially when combined with existing portal records or audit data.
assumptions: Assumes the portal stores or can query these attributes after receipt.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identification at the destination through received/stored data.

title: Disclosure from portal storage or processing of account-management data
description: Once received, the portal may expose names, emails, roles, account status changes, and parent-child relationships through excessive internal access, insecure storage, verbose logs, admin interfaces, or downstream integrations.
assumptions: Assumes the portal stores the submitted data or emits logs/events containing it.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure caused by destination-side storage/processing.

title: Unawareness of relationship and account-status processing
description: Parents, students, or even administrators may be unaware that the portal stores and processes parent-child links, role assignments, and account disablement history, including who changed what and when, and how long such data is retained or shared.
assumptions: Assumes notices, UI cues, or policy communication are incomplete or unclear.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for insufficient transparency/awareness at the destination.

title: Non-compliance from excessive or unjustified processing of relationship data
description: The portal may process or retain names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationships beyond what is necessary for account administration, without an appropriate legal basis, adequate retention limits, or sufficient safeguards for children's and family data.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy obligations exist for student/child and family relationship data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance due to purpose limitation, minimization, retention, or children's data obligations; exact node id may differ.

title: Repudiation of account or relationship changes due to inadequate evidence handling
description: If the portal does not maintain trustworthy, privacy-respecting audit trails for account creation, modification, disablement, and parent-child link changes, administrators may later deny having performed an action, or affected users may be unable to prove an unauthorized change occurred.
assumptions: Assumes audit logging may be incomplete, mutable, or not attributable to the acting administrator.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central than disclosure/linkability here; node id is a best estimate for destination-side repudiation.

title: Linkability of student and parent identities via stored relationship links
description: By storing parent-child relationship links together with account records, the account directory can enable linking multiple identities into family units and correlating student accounts with parent accounts across services or contexts.
assumptions: DS3 stores relationship links in a queryable or persistent form and can be accessed by other components or administrators beyond the immediate grading purpose.

assumptions: Account records contain names, usernames, email addresses, directory IDs, or other direct or indirect identifiers.

title: Disclosure of sensitive family relationship data in the account directory
description: The destination datastore may disclose sensitive personal data by retaining parent-child relationship links and account details, revealing family associations and educational context to unauthorized internal users, external attackers, or over-broad downstream consumers.
assumptions: DS3 is accessible to multiple systems, operators, or tenants, or lacks strict purpose-based access controls.

title: Unnecessary persistence of account and relationship data

assumptions: Not all written attributes or relationship links are strictly required for the directory's intended function, or retention periods are not limited.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for data minimization/excessive retention at the destination; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Excessive sharing of relationship data by the grading service
description: The grading service may write parent-child relationship links and account records to the directory even when only a subset of attributes is needed, causing disclosure of more personal data than necessary at the point of sharing.
assumptions: P2 has access to richer student/family data than DS3 strictly needs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for over-collection/over-sharing at the source; exact official node id may vary.

title: Secondary use of directory data beyond grading and account management
description: Once stored in the account directory, account records and family links may be reused for unrelated purposes such as analytics, profiling, contact campaigns, or access decisions without the data subjects' awareness or valid basis.
assumptions: DS3 serves multiple business functions or downstream consumers beyond the original grading workflow.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unauthorized/unexpected secondary use at the destination; exact node id may differ.

title: Insufficient transparency or legal basis for storing family links
description: Storing parent-child relationship links in the account directory may occur without adequate notice, consent where required, or another appropriate legal basis, especially if the directory's purpose is broader than educational grading operations.
assumptions: The system may be subject to privacy obligations requiring notice, purpose limitation, and lawful basis for processing children's and parents' data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance at the destination; exact official node id may vary.

title: Excessive disclosure through full backup replication
description: The source process sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to the cloud provider as part of nightly backup/replication. This may disclose more personal data than is necessary for hosting continuity, especially if entire records and directories are replicated rather than a minimized subset.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud hosting provider does not strictly need every field in the replicated dataset for the stated backup/hosting purpose.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for disclosure due to over-sharing/minimization failure; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Linkability created by consolidating grades, assignments, and directory data
description: By shipping full grade records together with assignment content and account directory information, the source enables straightforward linkage of academic performance, coursework, and identity/account attributes for the same individuals within the provider environment.
assumptions: Assumes the replicated datasets contain stable identifiers such as student IDs, usernames, email addresses, or similar account keys.

uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability due to direct/quasi-identifiers in disclosed data; exact node id may vary.

assumptions: Assumes repeated transfers expose stable metadata visible to the provider or network observers.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for linkability based on data-flow metadata rather than payload content.

assumptions: Assumes the system is subject to jurisdictional, educational-record, or contractual privacy requirements.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance related to storage location/retention/processor safeguards; exact node id may vary.

This creates a disclosure risk because sensitive educational data is shared from the datastore to the service.

This can enable profiling of data subjects and relationships between them.

The disclosure arises at the destination because P2 decides how much of the received data to expose onward.
